main_body: Snow-covered pitched roof (rows 7-50) over a timber plank front wall with an arched double door and two lit windows (rows 52-76)
top_band: Roof slope in white and pale blue snow clumps, rows ~8-50 in the middle column, ending in a bright snow lip at rows 47-50
evidence: The roof is a large foreshortened slope seen from above, as in the Beodeul house references, with a bright snow lip at rows 47-50 as the front edge. Directly below at row 52 the wall is in shadow under the eave and icicles. The wall is a separate vertical face with plank grain. The door has a dark inner edge and iron straps, and the windows have snow sills and dark frames, so the openings read as inset. There are no receding side faces.

style.evidence: The snow has about 5 lightness steps (white, pale, light blue-grey, mid blue, shadow) in scalloped clumps, which matches the reference roof tile rhythm. The wood wall has varied brown planks with grain, and the outlines lean brown or navy with the adjacent material rather than a uniform black line. The ornaments, icicles, moss patches and snow drifts at the base add dense detail per tile. No large flat fills appear.
